Playbook.name: AD — Object Security Descriptor Modified (DACL Backdoor) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An object's nTSecurityDescriptor was modified (5136) by a non-SYSTEM principal - attackers edit DACLs to grant themselves rights (GenericAll, DS-Replication, WriteDACL) on privileged objects for stealthy persistence. Triage question: legitimate delegation change, or a permission backdoor being planted?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A DACL edit granting rights over the domain root or a privileged group is persistent, low-noise domain control that survives password resets.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Delegation changes by identity admins during projects are legitimate; edits to the domain head / AdminSDHolder / privileged groups by an unexpected principal are backdoor shapes.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the DACL change is authorised delegation or a self-serving rights grant on a sensitive object.

Step.name: Which objects had descriptors changed by this principal
Step.Purpose: The sensitivity of the TARGET object (domain root, AdminSDHolder, Tier-0 groups) sets the severity.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "5136" AND winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "nTSecurityDescriptor" AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.ObjectDN, winlog.event_data.ObjectClass, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: ObjectDN = domain root, CN=AdminSDHolder, or a Tier-0 group/OU is high severity. Edits to a single delegated OU are lower concern.

Step.name: Is the actor concurrently doing other privileged directory changes
Step.Purpose: DACL edits combined with group/SPN/key changes indicate an active persistence campaign, not a one-off delegation.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("5136","4728","4732","4756","4742") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS ops = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), attrs = VALUES(winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple change types across objects by one principal in minutes = campaign; escalate regardless of the actor's nominal role.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a descriptor change on the domain root, AdminSDHolder, or a Tier-0 object by an unexpected principal.
INV-02 shows the actor concurrently changing groups/keys/delegation across objects.
INV-01 shows a scoped delegation change on a project OU by a known identity admin under change control.
Actor is a delegated admin but the target sensitivity/authorisation is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-DACL-OBJECTS, INV-02-DACL-CAMPAIGN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised delegation/permission management by an identity admin.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the delegation change; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A DACL edit planting persistent rights on a sensitive object.

Indicators.Item: Target is domain root / AdminSDHolder / Tier-0.
Actor unexpected or acting in a campaign.
Rights granted to the actor or a controlled account.

SOCAction.Item: Review and revert the ACL change; reset affected trustees.
Disable the actor, isolate its host, open IR.
Audit AdminSDHolder and domain-root ACLs fully.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A tool over-writing security descriptors due to misconfiguration.

Indicators.Item: Automation account re-applying descriptors per a broken template.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the tool; verify no excess rights were granted.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Capture and review the new ACL; revert unauthorised entries.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Audit domain-root/AdminSDHolder ACLs; reset trustees that gained rights.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Baseline and monitor ACLs on Tier-0 objects; restrict WriteDACL.

QualityChecks.Check: nTSecurityDescriptor edits are inherently sensitive - SYSTEM is excluded to cut noise.
Decoding the SDDL delta may require the AD team.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Backdoor ACL reverted; Tier-0 descriptors audited; actor eradicated.
